target_moa.text: Parathyroid hormone (rhPTH[1-84]) replacement; raises serum calcium by increasing renal tubular calcium reabsorption, increasing intestinal calcium absorption (via conversion of 25 OH vitamin D to 1,25 OH2 vitamin D), and increasing bone turnover that releases calcium into the circulation.

citations.quote: NATPARA is a parathyroid hormone. Parathyroid hormone raises serum calcium by increasing renal tubular calcium reabsorption, increasing intestinal calcium absorption (i.e., by converting 25 OH vitamin D to 1,25 OH2 vitamin D) and by increasing bone turnover which releases calcium into the circulation.
The active ingredient in Natpara® is synthetic rhPTH(1-84) and is identical to the full-length human 84-amino acid protein.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10%): paresthesia, hypocalcemia, headache, hypercalcemia, nausea, hypoaesthesia, diarrhea, vomiting, arthralgia, and pain in extremity. Severe hypercalcemia (in pivotal trial, 2 patients on NATPARA required IV fluids) and severe hypocalcemia (highest risk when NATPARA is withheld, missed or abruptly discontinued) have been reported.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions associated with NATPARA and occurring in greater than 10% of individuals were: paresthesia, hypocalcemia, headache, hypercalcemia, nausea, hypoaesthesia, diarrhea, vomiting, arthralgia, hypercalcemia and pain in extremity (6.1)
Severe hypercalcemia has been reported with NATPARA. In the pivotal trial, 2 patients randomized to NATPARA required administration of IV fluids to correct hypercalcemia.
Severe hypocalcemia has been reported with NATPARA. The risk is highest when NATPARA is withheld, missed or abruptly discontinued, but can occur at any time.

detail.text: WARNING: POTENTIAL RISK OF OSTEOSARCOMA — in male and female rats, parathyroid hormone caused a dose- and treatment-duration-dependent increase in the incidence of osteosarcoma (a malignant bone tumor); a risk to humans could not be excluded. Because of this risk, prescribe NATPARA only to patients who cannot be well-controlled on calcium and active vitamin D.

**WARNING: POTENTIAL RISK OF OSTEOSARCOMA**

detail.text: Because of the potential risk of osteosarcoma, NATPARA is available only through a restricted REMS program (NATPARA REMS Program) under which only certified healthcare providers can prescribe and only certified pharmacies can dispense NATPARA; ETASU include prescriber and pharmacy certification and documentation of safe use conditions.

Under the NATPARA REMS Program, only certified healthcare providers can prescribe and only certified pharmacies can dispense NATPARA. Further information is available at www.NATPARAREMS.com or by telephone at 1-855-NATPARA.

summary.text: NATPARA (rhPTH[1-84]) received traditional/full approval under a standard review as a BLA, based on the single pivotal placebo-controlled trial REPLACE whose primary composite responder endpoint was met. It had received Orphan Drug Designation for hypoparathyroidism in 2007, was presented at an advisory committee (September 12, 2014; vote 8-5), and was approved with a REMS and multiple post-marketing requirements to address the potential osteosarcoma and hypercalcemia risks.
